To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of a recomblinant soluble form of the MV hemagglutini (sH) and purified MV differ in their apparent binding affinity to CD46 under influence of SCR III/IV.
measles virus (MV), like soluble hemagglutinins (sH) derived from MV, binds to the external short consensus repeats (SCR I and SCR II) of the complement regulatory receptor, CD46.

the binding of a recomblent soluble form of the MV hemagglutini (sH) is enhanced by CD46 external SCR III and IV but inhibited by sH, and that sH and MV bind to CD46 SCR I and II, but with different avidity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the interaction of measles virus hemagglutini with its cellular receptor, CD46, and with the role of the different CD46 short consensus repeats in this process.
the identification of the CD46 domains involved in the interaction with the MV hemagglutinating protein.
the identification of the minimal CD46 binding domain of the MV hemagglutini.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding site for the sH is in CD46 SCR I and II, while the virus binds to a site in SCR I to III.
CD46 is a receptor for MV and that SCR I and II of CD46 are the minimal binding domain.
SCR I and II of CD46 are the binding domains of both MV and sH, but that SCR III and IV enhance the binding of MV to CD46.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CD46 SCR III and IV enhance MV binding but inhibit soluble hemagglutin binding to CD46.
SCR III and IV are important for MV attachment and that SCR I and II are important for sH binding.
the MV binding site on CD46 is located in SCR I and SCR II and that SCR III and SCR IV enhance MV binding but inhibit sH binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD46 binding site for the MV hemagglutini is composed of SCR I and II.
the MV binding site on the MV H protein is distinct from that on CD46.

the MV hemagglutinn is a multivalent molecule that binds CD46 through a combination of interactions with the SCR1 and SCR2 of CD46 and that the CD46 SCR3 and SCR4 are involved in the regulation of the avidity of MV to CD46.
